problem: “learns to use last” changes “longest in learning” (duration) into an ordering claim.
replacement: No one can deny that unrestrained liberty of association for political purposes is the privilege that takes a people longest to learn how to use. Even when it does not plunge the nation into anarchy, it keeps raising the chances of that disaster. On one point, however, this dangerous liberty protects against a different kind of danger: where associations are free, secret societies are unknown. In America there are numerous factions, but no conspiracies.

problem: “State” left capitalized where the style note requires lowercase “state” for the political body; also “far from the majority’s” softens “very much opposed”.
replacement: The difference between the Americans and ourselves depends on several causes. In Europe there are many parties so completely opposed to the majority that they can never hope to gain its support, and at the same time they think they are strong enough in themselves to struggle and to defend their cause. When a party of this kind forms an association, its object is not to conquer but to fight. In America, those whose opinions are very much opposed to the majority’s are no obstacle at all to its power, and all other parties hope in the end to win it over to their own principles. The exercise of the right of association becomes dangerous in proportion to how impossible it is for great parties to gain the majority. In a country like the United States, where differences of opinion are mere differences of shade, the right of association may remain unrestrained without bad consequences. Many European nations are inexperienced in the enjoyment of liberty, and this leads them to see the liberty of association only as a right to attack the government. The first idea that occurs to a party, as to an individual, once it has become conscious of its own strength, is that of violence. The idea of persuasion comes later and is learned only from experience. The English, who are divided into parties that differ most essentially from one another, rarely abuse the right of association, because they have long been used to exercising it. In France the passion for war is so intense that there is no undertaking so mad, or so harmful to the welfare of the state, that a man does not consider himself honored to defend it at the risk of his life.
